title: Stieger et al. 2021 — Continuous sensorimotor rhythm based brain computer interface learning in a large population
description: A large longitudinal dataset of sensorimotor rhythm-based brain-computer interface (BCI) training in 62 healthy adults. The dataset comprises over 600 hours of EEG recordings across 598 sessions with more than 250,000 trials of motor imagery tasks (left hand, right hand, both hands, and rest), collected during online continuous BCI control across up to 11 training sessions per participant. This resource enables investigation of BCI learning dynamics and algorithm development for non-invasive neural control applications.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired from 62 participants using Neuroscan SynAmps RT amplifiers with a 62-channel 10-10 montage at 1000 Hz sampling rate. Online preprocessing included 0.1-200 Hz bandpass filtering with 60 Hz notch filter. BCI control employed spatial filtering (Laplacian around C3/C4), autoregressive spectral estimation (order 16), and alpha power (12 ± 1.5 Hz) as the control signal. Each session consisted of 450 trials across 3 tasks (left-right, up-down, 2D cursor control) with 6 runs, where each trial included 2s inter-trial interval, 2s target presentation, and up to 6s feedback control with cursor position updates every 40 ms.
